dedupe_keys.name: convlstm based daily snow water equivalent swe predictions in us rocky mountains

description: The STARS4Water team deposits daily snow-water-equivalent predictions from a ConvLSTM model for the US Rocky Mountains. The own page says Daymet meteorological forcing trained and drove the model, with predictions compared against Daymet-derived snow-water estimates. It states a 0.04-degree grid and 2001 to 2009 coverage. Zenodo lists one public NetCDF of about 8.4 GB under CC BY 4.0. A mountain-basin hydrology or hydropower simulation could use the daily snow storage as a boundary or comparison series for seasonal runoff. These are model estimates, not independent snow surveys, and the reference uses a related Daymet-derived product. The landing page omits snow-water units, elevation handling, variable names and validation scores. The NetCDF was not downloaded, so time-axis completeness and masking remain unverified. No related catalogue record explicitly identifies this Rocky Mountains release.
